# @moku-labs/ai — full LLM reference

> A build system for AI-generated assets — declarative build files in, artifacts out.
> Any task × any provider × any account pool. Resumable always, incremental by default,
> never loses a byte of progress. Built on @moku-labs/core (Layer 2 of the three-layer
> Moku model). Version 0.14.2. Bun exclusively; Node >= 24, Bun >= 1.3.14.

Contents:
1. Architecture & factory chain
2. Public package surface
3. Core plugins: journal, store, limits (full types + APIs)
4. Regular plugins: registry, buildfile, runner, voiceover, translate, promptGen,
   image, video, elevenlabs, openai, codex, claude, compose, cli, asset, ark, music, fal,
   apimodels, sfx, sprite (full types + APIs)
5. Complete event catalog
6. Config schema (every field, type, default)
7. Complete usage examples
8. Error handling patterns
9. Plugin dependency graph + initialization order
10. Extension patterns (custom plugins)

================================================================================
1. ARCHITECTURE & FACTORY CHAIN
================================================================================

Layer 1 — src/config.ts:

```ts
export type Config = {};   // empty by ratified decision — all configuration is per-plugin
export type Events = {};   // empty — the runner declares its own events (register-callback pattern)

export const coreConfig = createCoreConfig<Config, Events, [
  typeof logPlugin, typeof envPlugin, typeof journalPlugin,
  typeof storePlugin, typeof limitsPlugin
]>("ai", {
  config: {},
  plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin, journalPlugin, storePlugin, limitsPlugin]
});

export const createPlugin = coreConfig.createPlugin; // framework-scoped plugin factory
export const createCore = coreConfig.createCore;     // framework assembler
```

Layer 2 — src/index.ts:

```ts
const framework = createCore(coreConfig, {
  plugins: [                                  // 21 regular plugins, dependency order
    registryPlugin, buildfilePlugin, runnerPlugin, voiceoverPlugin, translatePlugin,
    promptGenPlugin, imagePlugin, videoPlugin, musicPlugin, sfxPlugin, spritePlugin, assetPlugin,
    elevenlabsPlugin, openaiPlugin, codexPlugin, claudePlugin, falPlugin,
    apimodelsPlugin, arkPlugin, composePlugin, cliPlugin
  ],
  pluginConfigs: {
    env: { providers: [processEnv(), dotenv(".env.local")] }, // shell first, then .env.local
    limits: { lanes: {
      "video/apimodels": { concurrency: 2, rpm: 20 },
      "video/ark": { concurrency: 3, rpm: 180 }
    } }
  }
});
export const createApp = framework.createApp; // Layer-3 app factory
export const createPlugin = framework.createPlugin;
export function defineConfig<const P extends readonly AnyPluginInstance[] = readonly []>(
  config: ProjectConfig<P>): ProjectConfig<P>; // identity; types moku.config.ts
export { defineBuild } from "./plugins/buildfile";
// + plugin instances, helpers, type namespaces, <Provider>Errors (see §2)
```

Layer 3 — consumer apps (and src/bin.ts, the `moku` bin):

```ts
import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/ai";
const app = createApp({});           // options: { plugins?, config?, pluginConfigs?, onReady?, onError?, onStart?, onStop? }
await app.start();
// ... app.runner / app.voiceover / app.cli / app.limits ...
await app.stop();
```

The `moku` bin (src/bin.ts) is a Layer-3 consumer: loadProjectConfig
(src/plugins/cli/project-config.ts) → createApp(options) → start → cli.dispatch(argv) →
stop → process.exit(code). Project config:
- Discovery: the first of moku.config.ts, moku.config.mts, moku.config.js,
  moku.config.mjs in the cwd. No file → createApp({}).
- `--config <path>` or `--config=<path>` on any command wins over the search, resolves
  against the cwd, and is removed from argv before dispatch (the last one wins).
- The file's default export goes to createApp as is:
  `export default defineConfig({ plugins, pluginConfigs })`. Only `plugins` and
  `pluginConfigs` are allowed. defineConfig returns its argument; it types
  pluginConfigs, also for the custom plugins in `plugins` and for the core-plugin keys
  (journal, store, limits).
- A config that does not load exits 3 (usage) before any app exists: a missing
  `--config` file, a module that throws, a default export that is not an object
  (`[ai] Could not load <path>.\n  <reason>`), or `--config` with no path
  (`[ai] --config needs a file path.\n  Pass --config <path> or --config=<path>.`).

Key facts:
- Regular plugin APIs mount on the app BY NAME: app.registry, app.buildfile,
  app.runner, app.voiceover, app.translate, app.promptGen, app.image, app.video,
  app.music, app.sfx, app.sprite, app.asset, app.elevenlabs, app.openai, app.codex, app.claude, app.fal,
  app.apimodels, app.ark, app.compose, app.cli. Core APIs mount too (app.limits, ...).
  There is NO `app.plugins.<name>` indirection.
- App base methods: start(), stop(), emit(), require(), has(). There is NO `app.on` —
  bus-event subscription is a plugin concern (see §5, §10).
- Every regular plugin's ctx carries the injected core APIs: ctx.journal, ctx.store,
  ctx.limits, ctx.log, ctx.env.
- createApp's `pluginConfigs` is typed for REGULAR and CORE plugins (journal/store/limits,
  core >= 1.7.1). The framework sets env providers and two limits lanes at the
  createCore level (video/apimodels 2 concurrent / 20 rpm, video/ark 3 concurrent /
  180 rpm); journal and store keep their defaults. A `limits.lanes` override replaces
  the whole map.

2. PUBLIC PACKAGE SURFACE (@moku-labs/ai)
================================================================================

Value exports:
- createApp, createPlugin, defineConfig (type ProjectConfig), defineBuild
- Plugin instances: apimodelsPlugin, arkPlugin, assetPlugin, buildfilePlugin,
  claudePlugin, cliPlugin, codexPlugin, composePlugin, elevenlabsPlugin, falPlugin,
  imagePlugin, journalPlugin, limitsPlugin, musicPlugin, openaiPlugin, promptGenPlugin,
  registryPlugin, runnerPlugin, sfxPlugin, spritePlugin, storePlugin, translatePlugin,
  videoPlugin, voiceoverPlugin
- Error classes as runtime values, for `instanceof` (src/index.ts, `export * as`):
  ElevenlabsErrors, OpenaiErrors, ArkErrors, FalErrors, ApimodelsErrors (each
  RetryableProviderError, TerminalProviderError, FlaggedProviderError) and ClaudeErrors,
  CodexErrors (RetryableProviderError, TerminalProviderError; no flagged class).
  The same names under the plugin namespaces (`Fal.RetryableProviderError`, ...) are
  type aliases only: use them in annotations, never with `instanceof`.
- Cli.EXIT_CODES (const object)
- ASSET_MIME, encodeAssetRecord, parseAssetRecord (asset contract values)
- Type namespaces Asset (AssetRequest, AssetRecord, AssetResult, AssetJobPoll,
  AssetHandler, AssetFile, AssetGroupKind, AssetApi, Config) and Ark (Config, State,

- Type namespaces Music (MusicChunk, MusicRequest, MusicResult, MusicJobPoll,
  MusicHandler, MusicApi, MusicContext, Config, RegistryApi) and Fal (Config, State,
  UploadMode, FalApi, FalInfo, FalTask, FalModelInfo, LocalFile, RetryHint,
  FalProviderError, FalContext, EstimateInput, EstimateRequest, RegistryApi, error
  class types)
- Type namespaces Image (ImageFile, ImageHandler, ImageOutput, ImageRequest,
  ImageResult, Config, ImageApi, ImageContext, RegistryApi) and Video (EstimateInput,
  EstimateRequest, VideoFile, VideoHandler, VideoJobPoll, VideoRequest, VideoResult,
  Config, VideoApi, VideoContext, RegistryApi)
- Type namespaces Codex (Config, State, CodexInfo, CodexPromptMeta, CodexApi,
  CodexContext, RegistryApi, error class types) and Claude (Config, Reasoning, Effort,
  ClaudePromptMeta, ClaudeInfo, ClaudeApi, ClaudeContext, RegistryApi, error class types)
- Type namespaces Sfx (SfxRequest, SfxResult, SfxHandler, SfxApi, SfxContext, Config,
  RegistryApi) and Sprite (SpriteFile, SpriteRequest, SpriteResult, SpriteHandler,
  SpriteProcessOptions, ProcessedSprite, TrimBox, SpriteApi, SpriteContext, Config,
  RegistryApi). processSprite is not on the package root
- promptGen values: PromptGenUnavailableError (reason "missing" | "auth" | "limit" |
  "unsupported"), isPromptGenUnavailable, ToolArgumentsError (toolName, raw), and
  runToolLoop (the journaled tool loop; a library function, not a plugin — see §4.6)
- PromptGen namespace types: ContentPart, ChatMessage, ToolCall, ToolDefinition,
  PromptGenUsage, ToolSpec, ToolOutput, LoopEvent, RunToolLoopOptions, RunToolLoopResult
- apimodelsPlugin (plugin instance); type namespace Apimodels (Config, State,
  ApimodelsInfo, ApimodelsApi, ApimodelsProviderError, error class types)

Type namespaces (import type { X } from "@moku-labs/ai"; access as X.TypeName):
- Journal, Store, Limits, Buildfile, Runner, Voiceover, Translate, PromptGen, Image,
  Video, Music, Asset, Elevenlabs, Openai, Codex, Claude, Fal, Apimodels, Ark, Compose,
  Cli
(registry is Nano tier and ships no types.ts — its 4-method surface is declared once as
`RegistryApi` in `src/plugins/registry/index.ts`, and each dependent's types.ts
re-exports it: `export type { RegistryApi } from "../registry"`.)

Package entry: ESM + CJS with bundled .d.ts. Bin: `"moku": "./dist/bin.mjs"`.
Peer dependencies (install next to the package): @moku-labs/core ^1.7.1,
@moku-labs/common ^0.3.4. Dependencies: better-sqlite3 12.11.1, openai ^6.45.0,
sharp 0.35.5, yaml ^2.9.0, zod ^4.4.3.

================================================================================
3. CORE PLUGINS
================================================================================

Core plugins are registered in createCoreConfig (Layer 1). They declare no events, no
dependencies, and expose their APIs as ctx.* on every regular plugin's context and on
the app.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3.1 journal — ctx.journal (Complex tier)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Durable SQLite WAL ledger: one `runs` row per invocation, one `items` row per asset
(state machine queued → dispatching → done | failed | flagged), one `attempts` row per
provider call. Pragmas: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=FULL, fullfsync=1, busy_timeout;
every write inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Driver seam: bun:sqlite on Bun, better-sqlite3 on
Node (selected via `typeof Bun`). Metadata only — no payload columns exist, so prompts
and bodies are structurally impossible to journal. Lifecycle: onStart opens driver +
schema + checkpoint timer; onStop checkpoints and closes. API methods throw
"[ai] Journal is not open.\n  Call app.start() before using the journal." pre-start.

Types (src/plugins/journal/types.ts):

```ts
export type Config = {
  path: string;                 // default ".moku/journal.db"
  checkpointIntervalMs: number; // default 30_000 (wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) cadence; unref()'d timer)
  busyTimeoutMs: number;        // default 5000
};

export type State = {
  driver: SqliteDriver | null;                          // open connection; null until onStart
  checkpointTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null;
};

export type RunStatus = "active" | "done" | "failed" | "paused" | "budget-stopped";
export type ItemStatus = "queued" | "dispatching" | "done" | "failed" | "flagged";
export type ErrorClass =
  | "http-5xx" | "http-429" | "timeout" | "network" | "http-4xx" | "content-policy"
  | "invalid-request" | "local-failure" | "unknown";
export type AttemptOutcome = "done" | "retryable-error" | "terminal-error" | "flagged" | "aborted";
export type JobState = "submitted" | "done" | "failed" | "expired";
export type LiveJob = {
  externalId: string;                   // provider job id
  jobState: "submitted" | "expired";    // expired = a runner stopped waiting for it
  attemptId: number;                    // the attempt row the job was found on
};
export type DoneOutput = { contentHash: string; mimeType: string }; // one output of a multi-output item
export type DoneResult = {
  actualCostUsd: number; artifactKey: string;
  contentHash: string; mimeType?: string;  // the (first) artifact
  outputs?: DoneOutput[];                  // every output in order; absent for a single artifact
};
export type DoneArtifact = { contentHash: string; mimeType: string | null; outputs?: DoneOutput[] };

export type RunRow = {
  id: string;
  createdAt: number;
  status: RunStatus;
  glob: string;
  maxCostUsd: number | null;   // null = uncapped
  finishedAt: number | null;
};

export type ItemIntent = {
  planningKey: string;         // sha256(canonicalJson({ task, input, params }))
  buildFile: string;
  task: string;
  provider: string;
  packVersion: string | null;
  estimatedCostUsd: number;
  label: string;               // build item `id`, or `<NN>-<task>`; export file name
  buildName: string;           // the build file's `name`; export folder
  artifactKey: string;         // artifact identity, written at insert
};

export type ItemRow = Omit<ItemIntent, "artifactKey" | "label" | "buildName"> & {
  id: string;
  runId: string;
  status: ItemStatus;
  label: string | null;        // null only on rows written before labels existed
  buildName: string | null;    // null only on rows written before labels existed
  mimeType: string | null;     // of the committed artifact, when known
  outputs: DoneOutput[] | null; // multi-output item, in order; null for a single artifact
  artifactKey: string | null;
  contentHash: string | null;
  actualCostUsd: number | null;
  attemptCount: number;
  updatedAt: number;
};

export type GateResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: "budget" | "duplicate" };

export type RunTotals = {
  total: number; queued: number; dispatching: number; done: number;
  failed: number; flagged: number;
  spendUsd: number;               // sum of done items' actual cost
  estimatedRemainingUsd: number;  // sum of queued+dispatching estimates
};

export type AttemptStart = { provider: string; account: string; startedAt: number };
export type AttemptEnd = {
  endedAt: number; outcome: AttemptOutcome; errorClass?: ErrorClass; costUsd?: number;
};
export type RunSnapshot = { run: RunRow; totals: RunTotals; recentItems: ItemRow[] };
export type ItemFilter = { status?: ItemStatus; limit?: number; afterUpdatedAt?: number };
export type ProviderRecord = {         // one provider_records row; metadata only, never a body or key
  provider: string;                    // owning plugin, e.g. "apimodels"
  account: string;                     // non-reversible account fingerprint
  kind: string;                        // e.g. "asset" | "asset-group"
  key: string;                         // lookup key inside the kind, e.g. sha256 of the input bytes
  value: string;                       // opaque provider id, e.g. "asset://asset-1"
};
export type ProviderRecordQuery = Omit<ProviderRecord, "value">;

export type JournalApi = {
  openRun(opts: { glob: string; maxCostUsd?: number }): RunRow;
  getRun(runId: string): RunRow | undefined;
  latestResumableRun(opts?: { exclude?: readonly string[] }): RunRow | undefined;
    // newest "active" | "paused" | "budget-stopped" run whose id is not in exclude
  insertItems(runId: string, items: ItemIntent[]): ItemRow[];  // idempotent per (runId, planningKey)
  requeueDispatching(runId: string): number;  // crash-resume: dispatching → queued, returns count
  gateToDispatching(itemId: string): GateResult; // THE atomic budget+dedup gate (one transaction)
  recordAttempt(itemId: string, attempt: AttemptStart): number;
  finishAttempt(attemptId: number, end: AttemptEnd): void;
  commitDone(itemId: string, result: DoneResult): void;
  findDoneArtifact(artifactKey: string): DoneArtifact | undefined; // from any run
  reuseDone(itemId: string, artifact: DoneArtifact): void;
  setAttemptJob(attemptId: number, job: { externalId?: string; jobState: JobState }): void;
  findLiveJob(artifactKey: string): LiveJob | undefined;
  latestRun(): RunRow | undefined;
  getItem(runId: string, planningKey: string): ItemRow | undefined;
  markFailed(itemId: string, result: { errorClass: ErrorClass; terminal: boolean }): void;
    // terminal:true → failed; terminal:false → back to queued, attemptCount++
  markFlagged(itemId: string): void;          // content-policy terminal, never re-queued
  setRunStatus(runId: string, status: RunStatus): void; // terminal statuses record finishedAt
  totals(runId: string): RunTotals;
  listItems(runId: string, filter?: ItemFilter): ItemRow[]; // oldest-updated first
  readSnapshot(runId: string): RunSnapshot;   // own short-lived connection — safe from a 2nd process
  isOpen(): boolean;                          // true between onStart and onStop; the only method that never throws when closed
  findProviderRecord(q: ProviderRecordQuery): string | undefined; // the stored value, or undefined
  putProviderRecords(records: ProviderRecord[]): void; // upsert in ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; [] is a no-op
  deleteProviderRecord(q: ProviderRecordQuery): void;  // missing is a no-op
};
```

Schema (schema.ts): tables `runs`, `items` (UNIQUE (run_id, planning_key); index
(run_id, status)), `attempts`, `provider_records`. Created idempotently on onStart.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3.2 store — ctx.store (Standard tier)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Content-addressed store on the local filesystem. Objects at {dir}/{hash[0..2]}/{hash}.
Write protocol: unique tmp file in the shard dir → fsync(file) → rename(tmp, final) →
fsync(parent dir). First-committer-wins dedup (existing hash = no-op success; EEXIST on
rename = success). Reads recompute the hash and throw on mismatch. Hashes are validated
64-char lowercase sha256 hex (blocks path traversal). No lifecycle hooks; root dir is
created lazily on first put. The store dir is gitignored (may embed prompts/PII).

Types (src/plugins/store/types.ts):

```ts
export type Config = {
  dir: string;      // default ".moku/store"
  algo: "sha256";   // fixed at M0; forward-compat option
};
export type State = { rootEnsured: boolean };
export type PutResult = { hash: string; path: string; existed: boolean };
export type GcResult = { removed: number; bytesFreed: number };

export type StoreApi = {
  put(content: Uint8Array): Promise<PutResult>;   // durable when resolved
  has(hash: string): Promise<boolean>;
  pathOf(hash: string): string;                    // sync; throws not-found
  read(hash: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;         // integrity re-verified on every read
  hashOf(content: Uint8Array): string;             // hash without writing (planning-time identity)
  gc(keep: ReadonlySet<string>): Promise<GcResult>; // sweep everything not in keep; skips .tmp-*
};
```

Pinned errors: "[ai] Store object not found for hash <hash>." and
"[ai] Store integrity check failed for <hash>." (corrupt object — delete + re-run).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3.3 limits — ctx.limits (Standard tier)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Per-lane admission control; lane key "{task}/{provider}/{account}" (account is always
"default" at M0). Three independent guards per lane: token bucket (rpm), FIFO
concurrency gate, circuit breaker (opens after breakerThreshold consecutive retryable
failures; half-open single-probe after breakerCooldownMs; any outcome settles the
probe). Timer-free: refill/breaker transitions are lazy timestamp math. Lane state is
created lazily on first acquire/reportOutcome. Pending waiters die with the process —
safe because gated work stays journal-queued/dispatching and resumes.

Types (src/plugins/limits/types.ts):

```ts
export type LaneConfig = {
  rpm: number;               // default 60 (also bucket capacity)
  concurrency: number;       // default 4
  breakerThreshold: number;  // default 5
  breakerCooldownMs: number; // default 30_000
};
export type Config = {
  defaults: LaneConfig;
  lanes: Record<string, Partial<LaneConfig>>; // keys: exact lane OR "{task}/{provider}" prefix
};
export type LaneState = {
  tokens: number; lastRefillAt: number; inFlight: number;
  waiters: Array<() => void>; consecutiveFailures: number;
  openUntil: number; probing: boolean;
};
export type State = { lanes: Map<string, LaneState> };
export type LaneSnapshot = {
  lane: string; tokens: number; inFlight: number; waiting: number;
  breaker: "closed" | "open" | "half-open";
};

export type LimitsApi = {
  acquire(lane: string, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<{ release: () => void }>;
    // waits: breaker closed (or probe slot) → token → concurrency slot (FIFO).
    // release() must be called exactly once (no-op after the first).
    // Rejects IMMEDIATELY with an Error tagged `reason: "breaker-open"` when open.
    // Abort during the wait rejects with signal.reason; nothing leaks (token refunded,
    // waiter dequeued, probe slot released).
  reportOutcome(lane: string, outcome: "ok" | "retryable-error"): void;
    // "ok" closes/resets; "retryable-error" advances toward open.
    // Do NOT report terminal 4xx — deterministic, not a health signal. Never throws.
  laneConfig(lane: string): LaneConfig;   // exact > prefix > defaults; pure lookup
  snapshot(lane: string): LaneSnapshot;   // lazily refills before reading; untouched lane = pristine
  lanes(): string[];                       // lanes touched by at least one acquire/reportOutcome
};
```

================================================================================
4. REGULAR PLUGINS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.1 registry — app.registry (Nano tier; no config, no events, no types.ts)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dumb two-level map: task → provider → handler, stored/returned as `unknown` — the
registry never inspects what it transports. Provider plugins register in onInit via
ctx.require(registryPlugin); task plugins resolve + guard + perform their ONE audited
cast. PERMANENT CONSTRAINT: must stay a regular plugin (core-plugin ctx has no
require/depends, and providers need `depends: [registryPlugin]`).

```ts
// API (inferred; declared once as RegistryApi in registry/index.ts, re-exported by dependents)
register(task: string, provider: string, handler: unknown): void;
  // throws on duplicate: `[ai] Provider "<provider>" is already registered for task "<task>".
  //   Register each task/provider pair exactly once.`
resolve(task: string, provider: string): unknown;   // undefined when unregistered; never throws
providers(task: string): string[];  // registration order; [0] is the task's default provider
tasks(): string[];                  // registration order
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.2 buildfile — app.buildfile (Standard tier; stateless pure compiler; no deps)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The build-file front door: parses *.moku.yaml and defineBuild() TS modules through ONE
zod schema (schema.ts). BuildSpec/BuildItem are z.infer of the zod objects; the JSON
Schema is z.toJSONSchema of the same objects — validator, static types, and editor
autocomplete can never drift. Deliberately does NOT consult registry (provider
existence is checked by the runner at dispatch) — `moku validate` works offline.

Types (src/plugins/buildfile/types.ts):

```ts
export type BuildItem = z.infer<typeof buildItemSchema>;
// = { task: string; id?: string; provider?: string; input: Record<string, unknown>;
//     params?: Record<string, unknown>; pack?: { name: string; version: string } }
export type BuildSpec = z.infer<typeof buildSpecSchema>;
// = { version: 1; name: string; defaults?: { provider?: string; maxAttempts?: number };
//     items: BuildItem[]; itemsFrom?: string }
export type Config = {
  defaultGlob: string;  // default "**/*.moku.yaml"
  schemaPath: string;   // default ".moku/build.schema.json"
};
export type CompiledBuild = { file: string; spec: BuildSpec }; // file = path or "<inline>"
export type BuildfileSource = { path: string } | { text: string; lang: "yaml" };

export type BuildfileApi = {
  compile(source: BuildfileSource): Promise<CompiledBuild>;
    // .ts path → dynamic import, default export must be a defineBuild() result;
    // other paths → YAML. itemsFrom NDJSON (resolved relative to the build file) is
    // appended to spec.items at compile time.
    // throws: `[ai] Build file "<label>" is invalid.\n  <zod path>: <message>.`
  loadGlob(pattern?: string): Promise<CompiledBuild[]>;  // sorted path order
    // empty match throws: `[ai] No build files matched "<pattern>".\n  Run "moku new" to create one.`
  jsonSchema(): Record<string, unknown>;
  template(opts: { name: string }): string;
    // modeline + $schema: key + minimal valid spec + one commented example per M0 task
};
```

Standalone helper (also re-exported from "@moku-labs/ai"):

```ts
export function defineBuild(spec: BuildSpec): BuildSpec;
// pure factory; validates through the exact schema the YAML loader uses
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.3 runner — app.runner (Complex tier; depends: [registryPlugin, buildfilePlugin])
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The durable orchestrator. Per-item pipeline:
1. Plan — buildfile.loadGlob(files); order items by $ref; resolve provider (item.provider →
   defaults.provider → registry.providers(task)[0]); planning key =
   sha256(canonicalJson({ task, input, params })) (provider excluded; $ref → target planning
   key, $file → file sha256); artifact key = same over { task, provider, packVersion, input,
   params } ($ref → target artifact key); request = { ...input, params }; estimate via
   handler.estimate(request); journal.insertItems as queued with label/buildName/artifactKey.
1a. Reuse — journal.findDoneArtifact(artifactKey) from ANY run, bytes in store → reuseDone
   ($0, no provider call).
1b. References — wait for $ref targets; not done → item stays queued, run ends paused;
   $ref/$file resolve to { path, mimeType, hash }.
2. Admit — limits.acquire("{task}/{provider}/default", { signal }); abort/breaker-open
   exits cleanly (item stays queued).
3. Gate — journal.gateToDispatching(itemId): budget + dedup + transition in ONE
   transaction. "budget" → graceful budget-stop drain; "duplicate" → release slot.
4. Execute — registry.resolve(task, provider) narrowed by isExecutableHandler() (the
   runner's single audited cast); journal.recordAttempt; submit+poll when the handler has both
   (job id journaled via setAttemptJob before any wait; a live job for the same artifact key
   is adopted, never re-submitted; poll every pollIntervalMs; expired after jobTimeoutMs),
   else handler.execute(request, { signal }).
5. Classify — classifyError maps thrown errors onto the taxonomy;
   limits.reportOutcome("ok" | "retryable-error").
6. Persist — normalize (body | audio | image | video | text), store.put(bytes) THEN
   journal.commitDone(itemId, { actualCostUsd, artifactKey, contentHash, mimeType }).
7. Report — item record to events() subscribers; coalesced run:progress on the bus.

Named constraints: per-item events NEVER on the bus; redaction boundary (raw
prompts/bodies never reach ctx.journal — HandlerRequest is never journaled); up to
maxActiveRuns runs per process (default 1; above the cap run()/resume() throws);
lanes are shared across runs; the same artifact key in two runs is submitted once;
app.stop() pauses active runs (onStop) and waits for them before the journal closes.

Types (src/plugins/runner/types.ts):

```ts
export type Config = {
  maxAttempts: number;     // default 3 (per build file overridable via defaults.maxAttempts)
  retryBaseMs: number;     // default 1000 (exponential, jittered 50–100%; Retry-After honored when larger)
  eventBufferSize: number; // default 10_000 (events() per-consumer buffer)
  pollIntervalMs: number;  // default 5000
  jobTimeoutMs: number;    // default 1_800_000
  maxActiveRuns: number;   // default 1 (runs driven at once in this process)
};

export type RunOptions = { files?: string; maxCostUsd?: number; dryRun?: boolean };
export type RunResultStatus = "done" | "failed" | "paused" | "budget-stopped";
export type RunResult = { runId: string; status: RunResultStatus; totals: RunTotals };
export type EstimateLine = { task: string; provider: string; items: number; usd: number };
export type EstimateResult = { lines: EstimateLine[]; totalUsd: number };
export type RunStatusReport = { runId: string; status: string; totals: RunTotals; updatedAt: number };

export type RunEvent =                     // every record carries runId
  | { type: "item:queued"; runId: string; itemId: string; task: string; provider: string }
  | { type: "item:dispatching"; runId: string; itemId: string }
  | { type: "item:done"; runId: string; itemId: string; costUsd: number;
      contentHash: string;                  // the item's (first) artifact
      contentHashes?: string[] }            // every output in order; multi-output items only
  | { type: "item:retry"; runId: string; itemId: string; errorClass: ErrorClass; attempt: number }
  | { type: "item:failed"; runId: string; itemId: string;
      label: string | null;                 // ItemRow.label; null only on rows written before labels existed
      errorClass: ErrorClass;
      message?: string }                    // first two lines (max 300 chars) of the handler's
                                            // publicMessage, else of our own [ai] error; else absent
  | { type: "item:flagged"; runId: string; itemId: string; message?: string } // same message rule
  | { type: "overflow"; runId: string; dropped: number }
  | { type: "progress"; runId: string; totals: RunTotals }
  | { type: "terminal"; runId: string; status: RunResultStatus; totals: RunTotals };

export type RunnerEvents = {
  "run:progress": { runId: string; total: number; done: number; failed: number;
                    flagged: number; spendUsd: number };
  "run:done": { runId: string; totals: RunTotals };
  "run:failed": { runId: string; error: string };
  "run:budget-stop": { runId: string; spendUsd: number; maxCostUsd: number };
  "run:paused": { runId: string; drained: number };
};

export type HandlerRequest = Record<string, unknown>; // { ...item.input, params }
export type ResolvedFile = { path: string; mimeType: string; hash: string };
export type HandlerResult = {
  body?: Uint8Array; audio?: Uint8Array; image?: Uint8Array; video?: Uint8Array; text?: string;
  mimeType?: string;
  images?: { image: Uint8Array; mimeType: string }[]; // every image of a multi-image result, in order; each one stored
  costUsd: number; meta?: Record<string, unknown>;
};
export type JobPoll =
  | { state: "pending" }
  | ({ state: "done" } & HandlerResult)
  | { state: "failed"; error: unknown };
export type ExecutableHandler = {
  estimate(request: HandlerRequest): { usd: number };
  execute?(request: HandlerRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<HandlerResult>;
  submit?(request: HandlerRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<{ jobId: string }>;
  poll?(jobId: string, request: HandlerRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<JobPoll>;
};
export type ExportResult = {
  runId: string; outDir: string; skipped: string[];
  files: Array<{ label: string; path: string; bytes: number; costUsd: number; mimeType: string }>;
};
export type ProviderErrorHint = {
  status?: number;
  kind?:
    | "timeout" | "network" | "content-policy" // override status-based inference
    | "resubmit"          // keeps the status class; keeps the failure off the lane breaker
    | "invalid-request"   // the handler refuses the request: failed after one attempt, no breaker outcome
    | "local-failure";    // the handler's own machine failed: same as invalid-request
  retryAfterMs?: number;  // honored when larger than the computed backoff
  publicMessage?: string; // safe-to-show text; item:failed / runner:item:failed carry its first
                          // two lines (max 300 chars); never journaled
};
// A poll error with no hint, or kind "invalid-request" / "local-failure", marks the job
// expired so the next run adopts it. A "resubmit" verdict must be returned from poll as
// { state: "failed", error }; a thrown one is read as pending.

export type State = {
  active: Map<string, ActiveRun>;
  subscribers: Set<Subscriber>;
  claims: Map<string, Claim>; // artifact key -> the item allowed to reach the provider
};

export type RunnerApi = {
  run(options: RunOptions, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal; onStart?: (runId: string) => void }): Promise<RunResult>;
    // dryRun → no journal writes, runId "dry-run", status "done", plan total in
    // totals.estimatedRemainingUsd. Throws only above maxActiveRuns;
    // in-run failures resolve { status: "failed" } after emitting run:failed.
  resume(opts?: { runId?: string; signal?: AbortSignal; onStart?: (runId: string) => void }): Promise<RunResult>;
    // requeueDispatching + idempotent re-plan; done items never re-billed.
  estimate(options: { files?: string }): Promise<EstimateResult>; // same math as the budget gate
  status(runId?: string): RunStatusReport; // given id, else active run, else latest resumable
  events(opts?: { runId?: string }): AsyncIterable<RunEvent>;
    // { runId }: that run only; no runId: every run until none is active. Every record carries runId.
    // per-consumer bounded queue; oldest ITEM records drop into one {type:"overflow"};
    // "progress" coalesces (latest wins); "terminal" is ALWAYS delivered last.
  export(opts?: { runId?: string; outDir?: string; flat?: boolean }): Promise<ExportResult>;
    // runId default: newest run; outDir default "out"; flat default false.
    // Writes <outDir>/<build name>/<label>.<ext>, or <outDir>/<label>.<ext> with flat: true
    // (no build folder; the build name is not checked). label = item id, else <NN>-<task>.
    // A multi-output item adds <label>-2.<ext> … <label>-N.<ext> (cost on the first file).
    // An unsafe label, or a target this export already wrote (with flat: the same label in
    // two builds), is skipped and listed in `skipped`; the first file is kept.
};
```

Retry taxonomy (contractual): http-5xx (status>=500) retry · http-429 retry
(Retry-After honored when larger) · timeout (kind) retry · network (kind) retry ·
http-4xx (except 429) terminal failed · unknown (no hint) terminal failed after one
attempt · content-policy (kind) terminal flagged.

4.4 voiceover — app.voiceover (Standard tier; depends: [registryPlugin]; stateless)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Owns the "voiceover" task contract; providers implement + register it; this plugin
resolves, runtime-shape-guards, and performs the task's ONE audited cast. Also bundles
versioned template packs (packs/narration.ts): per-provider param presets merged UNDER
request params (request wins); pack version participates in artifact identity.

Contract (src/plugins/voiceover/contract.ts):

```ts
export type VoiceoverRequest = {
  text: string;
  voice: string;                     // provider-scoped voice id/name
  language?: string;                 // BCP-47 hint
  model?: string;
  format?: "mp3" | "wav" | "ogg";    // defaulted from config.defaultFormat when omitted
  params?: Record<string, unknown>;  // resolved pack values merged upstream
};
export type VoiceoverResult = {
  audio: Uint8Array;
  mimeType: string;                  // audio/mpeg | audio/wav | audio/ogg
  costUsd: number;
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;    // metadata only — never a payload echo
};
export type VoiceoverHandler = {
  estimate(request: VoiceoverRequest): { usd: number };
  execute(request: VoiceoverRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<VoiceoverResult>;
};
```

Config + API (src/plugins/voiceover/types.ts):

```ts
export type Config = {
  defaultProvider: string;              // default "elevenlabs"
  defaultFormat: "mp3" | "wav" | "ogg"; // default "mp3"
};
export type VoiceoverApi = {
  generate(request: VoiceoverRequest,
    opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal; provider?: string }): Promise<VoiceoverResult>; // NOT journaled
  estimate(request: VoiceoverRequest, opts?: { provider?: string }): { usd: number };

```

4.6 promptGen — app.promptGen (Standard tier; depends: [registryPlugin]; stateless)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NAMING: plugin/api name is camelCase `promptGen`; the registry/task key used in build
files and register() calls is kebab-case `"prompt-gen"`. Exists at M0 primarily to back
`compose` (which calls this facade instead of touching the registry).

Contract (src/plugins/promptGen/contract.ts):

```ts
export type ContentPart =
  | { type: "text"; text: string; cache?: true }                       // cache: a cache breakpoint after this part
  | { type: "image"; path: string; mimeType: string; hash: string };   // same shape as params.images
export type ChatMessage =
  | { role: "user"; content: string | ContentPart[] }
  | { role: "assistant"; content: string | null; toolCalls?: ToolCall[] }
  | { role: "tool"; toolCallId: string; content: string | ContentPart[] };
export type ToolCall = { id: string; name: string; input: unknown };  // input: parsed JSON arguments
export type ToolDefinition = { name: string; description: string; inputSchema: Record<string, unknown> };
export type PromptGenRequest = {
  prompt: string;                    // ignored when messages is set (may be "")
  system?: string;
  model?: string;
  temperature?: number;              // provider maps/clamps as needed
  params?: Record<string, unknown>;
  messages?: ChatMessage[];          // the turns after system; replaces prompt
  tools?: ToolDefinition[];
  toolChoice?: "auto" | "none" | "required" | { name: string };   // default "auto"
  cacheSystem?: boolean;             // a cache breakpoint after the system text
};
export type PromptGenUsage = {
  promptTokens: number; completionTokens: number;
  cachedTokens: number;              // 0 when unknown
  cacheWriteTokens: number;          // 0 when unknown
  cachedReadTokens?: number;         // set only when the provider reports it
  cachedWriteTokens?: number;        // set only when the provider reports it
};
export type PromptGenResult = {
  text: string;                      // "" when the turn is only tool calls
  costUsd: number;
  toolCalls: ToolCall[];             // [] when none
  finishReason: "stop" | "tool_calls" | "length" | "other";
  usage: PromptGenUsage;
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;    // keeps its keys for compatibility
};
export type PromptGenHandler = {
  estimate(request: PromptGenRequest): { usd: number };
  execute(request: PromptGenRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<PromptGenResult>;
};
export class PromptGenUnavailableError extends Error {
  readonly unavailable = true;
  readonly reason: "missing" | "auth" | "limit" | "unsupported";
}
export class ToolArgumentsError extends Error { readonly toolName: string; readonly raw: string }
export function isPromptGenUnavailable(error: unknown): boolean; // unavailable === true, or status 401/402/403/429
```

toolCalls, finishReason and usage are REQUIRED: a PromptGenHandler outside this repo must
return them (a one-turn handler: toolCalls [], finishReason "stop", its token counts or 0).
A request without messages, tools, toolChoice and cacheSystem is sent exactly as before.
claude, codex and openai throw PromptGenUnavailableError reason "unsupported" for
messages/tools/toolChoice in estimate() and execute(); cacheSystem alone is ignored there.
generate then falls back to the next provider; fal serves them (see §4.18 fal). estimate has
no fallback: estimate a tool request with { provider: "fal" }. ToolArgumentsError is not
"unavailable": generate rethrows it at once.

```ts
export type Config = { defaultProvider: string; fallback: string[] }; // defaults "openai", []
export type PromptGenApi = {
  generate(request: PromptGenRequest,
    opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal; provider?: string }): Promise<PromptGenResult>; // NOT journaled
  estimate(request: PromptGenRequest, opts?: { provider?: string }): { usd: number };
  providers(): string[];
};
```

runToolLoop (src/plugins/promptGen/loop/; exported from the package root; a library
function, not a plugin; calls only options.generate):

```ts
export type ToolOutput<O = unknown> = { value: O; content: ContentPart[]; costUsd: number; rows?: string[] };
export type ToolSpec<I = unknown, O = unknown> = {
  name: string; description: string;
  schema: z.ZodType<I>;                       // checks input; z.toJSONSchema(io "input") without $schema in the request
  estimateUsd?(input: I): number;             // for the breaker; absent = 0, no check
  run(input: I, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ToolOutput<O>>;
  start?(input: I, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<{ started: unknown; rows?: string[] }>;  // JSON-safe
  wait?(started: unknown, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ToolOutput<O>>;                  // both set → used instead of run
};
export type LoopEvent =
  | { kind: "model"; step: number; text: string | null; toolCalls: ToolCall[]; costUsd: number; usage: PromptGenUsage }
  | { kind: "tool"; step: number; name: string; callId: string; costUsd: number; summary: string; rows: string[] }
  | { kind: "budget"; spentUsd: number; limitUsd: number; mode: "finish" | "stop" };
export type RunToolLoopOptions = {
  generate: (request: PromptGenRequest, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<PromptGenResult>;
  model: string; reasoning?: "off" | "low" | "medium" | "high";
  system: string; messages: ChatMessage[]; tools: readonly ToolSpec[];
  budget: { usd: number; spentUsd?: number; finishAt: number; spent?: () => Promise<number> };
  maxSteps: number;
  step: <T>(key: string, work: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<{ value: T; costUsd: number }>) => Promise<T>;
  onStep?: (event: LoopEvent) => void;
  finishNote?: string; keepImages?: number;  // keepImages default 2
  cache?: "system" | "conversation" | "off";  // default "conversation": system mark + up to two rolling cache: true marks on the newest stable user/tool message; max 4 breakpoints with caller marks
  signal: AbortSignal;
};
export type RunToolLoopResult = {
  stoppedBy: "done" | "budget" | "steps" | "cancel" | "asked";
  spentUsd: number; steps: number; messages: ChatMessage[]; finalText: string | null;
  asked?: { input: unknown };
};
export function runToolLoop(options: RunToolLoopOptions): Promise<RunToolLoopResult>;
```

- Request per model call: { prompt: "", system, model, messages, tools, cacheSystem: true }
  plus params: { reasoning } when set.
- Journal steps: model:<n> (value: PromptGenResult), tool:<callId> (value: ToolOutput), or
  tool:<callId>:start ({ started, rows }, cost 0) then tool:<callId>:wait (ToolOutput). A
  replayed key calls nothing; values carry their cost, so a replay rebuilds spentUsd.
- spent = budget.spentUsd + every step's cost + await budget.spent(). Before a model call:
  abort, then steps >= maxSteps → "steps", then spent >= usd → "budget". Before a tool with
  estimateUsd: spent + estimate > usd → "budget", tool not run. Both emit budget "stop".
- Finish mode: the first time spent >= finishAt × usd → budget "finish" once; finishNote joins
  as a user message before the next model call unless a user message already equals it.
- A "budget", "steps" or "cancel" stop answers every open call of the last assistant turn
  with "Not run: <reason>.". "asked" leaves the ask call open; the caller appends
  { role: "tool", toolCallId, content } with the person's answer.
- Unknown tool → 'Unknown tool "<name>".'; zod failure → "Invalid input for <name>:
  <z.prettifyError>"; content [] → "(no output)". Each one step, cost 0.
- A tool named "ask" (defined by the caller) is never run: the other calls of the turn run,
  then stoppedBy "asked" with asked.input. keepImages: tool-result images older than the last
  N assistant turns become "[image dropped: <file name>]" in the request only.
- A tool or generate error propagates; when the signal is aborted it is "cancel" instead.
- Caveats: a continued conversation needs a new journal key space (keys restart at model:1);
  result.spentUsd already includes budget.spent(); call ids must be unique across turns.
- Full guide: src/plugins/promptGen/README.md "Tool loop — runToolLoop".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.7 image — app.image (Standard tier; depends: [registryPlugin]; stateless)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Owns the "image" task contract (still images); providers implement + register it; this
plugin resolves, runtime-shape-guards (estimate and execute must be functions) and
performs the task's ONE audited cast. No state, no lifecycle, no events, no packs. The
runner never calls this facade; it drives the registered handlers directly. Providers in
registration order: codex (the default), fal, ark. contract.ts imports nothing.

Contract (src/plugins/image/contract.ts; `Image.*` namespace):

```ts
export type ImageFile = {           // a resolved $ref / $file input
  path: string;
  mimeType: string;                  // e.g. image/png
  hash: string;                      // content hash: artifact identity follows the bytes
};
export type ImageRequest = {
  prompt: string;                    // what to draw; the caller already appended the series style
  negative?: string;                 // things to avoid
  model?: string;                    // provider-scoped model id
  aspect?: string;                   // e.g. "9:16"; providers default to "9:16"
  refs?: ImageFile[];                // character sheet, location plate, earlier keyframe
  params?: Record<string, unknown>;  // pass-through provider params
};
export type ImageOutput = { image: Uint8Array; mimeType: string }; // one image of a group
export type ImageResult = {
  image: Uint8Array;
  mimeType: string;                  // e.g. image/png, image/webp
  images?: ImageOutput[];            // every image of a group, in order; images[0] is image; absent for one image
  costUsd: number;
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;    // metadata only — never a payload echo
};
export type ImageHandler = {
  estimate(request: ImageRequest): { usd: number };
  execute(request: ImageRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<ImageResult>;
};
```

Groups: a provider that makes several consistent images in one call (ark Seedream with
params.images) returns all of them in `images` and the first again as image / mimeType.
The runner stores every entry and journals them as the item's ordered outputs; export
writes <label>.<ext>, <label>-2.<ext> … <label>-N.<ext>; a $ref to the item is the first
image. generate() passes the result through unchanged.

Config + API (src/plugins/image/types.ts):

```ts
export type Config = { defaultProvider: string }; // default "codex"
export type ImageApi = {
  generate(request: ImageRequest,
    opts?: { provider?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<ImageResult>; // NOT journaled
  estimate(request: ImageRequest, opts?: { provider?: string }): { usd: number };
  providers(): string[]; // = registry.providers("image"), registration order
};
```

Unknown-provider error (also for a registered value that is not an ImageHandler):
`[ai] No image provider named "<name>" is registered.\n  Available: <list or "none">.`

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.8 video — app.video (Standard tier; depends: [registryPlugin]; stateless)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Owns the "video" task contract; providers implement + register it; this plugin exposes a
one-off facade. A handler has `estimate` plus either `execute`, or the async pair
`submit` + `poll` (or both). The runner prefers `submit`/`poll` and journals the job id,
so a resume polls the live job and never re-submits; the facade `generate` prefers
`execute`, else submits once and polls in memory every `pollIntervalMs`. The ONE audited
cast is behind `isVideoHandler` (module export, not on app.video). No state, no lifecycle,
no events. Providers in registration order: fal (the default), apimodels, ark.
contract.ts imports nothing.

Contract (src/plugins/video/contract.ts; `Video.*` namespace):

```ts
export type VideoFile = { path: string; mimeType: string; hash: string };
export type VideoRequest = {
  model: string;           // provider-scoped id or alias; REQUIRED: price and endpoint depend on it
  prompt: string;          // motion and scene prompt
  negative?: string;       // ignored by models without a negative prompt
  image?: VideoFile;       // first frame / keyframe
  endImage?: VideoFile;    // last frame; a model without one rejects the request before any upload or charge
  refs?: VideoFile[];      // images, audio or video files, told apart by MIME type
  seconds?: number;        // default 5
  aspect?: string;         // default "9:16"
  resolution?: string;     // model-specific, e.g. "720p", "768P"
  audio?: boolean;         // native audio when the model can; default false
  params?: Record<string, unknown>; // pass-through, merged last into the provider body
  fromDraft?: VideoFile;   // the draft clip this request renders as a final (pass prompt "" from code)
};
export type EstimateInput = VideoFile | { $ref: string } | { $file: string };
export type EstimateRequest = Omit<VideoRequest, "image" | "endImage" | "refs" | "fromDraft"> & {
  image?: EstimateInput; endImage?: EstimateInput; refs?: EstimateInput[]; fromDraft?: EstimateInput;
};                         // estimate runs at plan time, before references resolve; every VideoRequest is one
export type VideoResult = {
  video: Uint8Array;
  mimeType: string;        // e.g. video/mp4
  costUsd: number;
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>; // metadata only — never a payload echo
};
export type VideoJobPoll =
  | { state: "pending" }
  | ({ state: "done" } & VideoResult)
  | { state: "failed"; error: unknown };
export type VideoHandler = {
  estimate(request: EstimateRequest): { usd: number };
  execute?(request: VideoRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<VideoResult>;
  submit?(request: VideoRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<{ jobId: string }>;
  poll?(jobId: string, request: VideoRequest, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<VideoJobPoll>;
};
```

isVideoHandler(candidate: unknown) (video/api.ts) is the runtime guard: estimate is a
function, and execute is, or submit and poll both are.

Draft → final (only ark, Seedance 2.5): the draft item sets params.draft: true; the final
item sets input.fromDraft: { $ref: <draft item> } and may omit prompt. The provider reuses
the draft's prompt, frames, duration, ratio, seed and audio; the final renders at 1080p
only; draft ids expire after 7 days. Providers without a draft mode refuse fromDraft.

Config + API (src/plugins/video/types.ts):

```ts
export type Config = {
  defaultProvider: string; // default "fal"
  pollIntervalMs: number;  // default 5000 (facade only; the runner uses runner.pollIntervalMs)
};
export type VideoApi = {
  // One-off, NOT journaled. execute when present; else submit once, poll every
  // config.pollIntervalMs; done → the result without `state`; a failed poll throws its
  // error as-is; abort during the wait rejects at once with the signal's reason.
  generate(request: VideoRequest,
    opts?: { provider?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<VideoResult>;
  estimate(request: VideoRequest, opts?: { provider?: string }): { usd: number };
  providers(): string[];   // = registry.providers("video"), registration order
};
```

Unknown-provider error (also for a value that fails isVideoHandler):
`[ai] No video provider named "<name>" is registered.\n  Available: <list or "none">.`

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.9 elevenlabs — app.elevenlabs (Complex tier; depends: [registryPlugin])
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Provider adapter for ElevenLabs. Thin fetch client, no SDK. onInit registers
("voiceover", "elevenlabs") → createVoiceoverHandler(ctx) and ("sfx", "elevenlabs") →
createSfxHandler(ctx) (§4.20). POST
/v1/text-to-speech/{voiceId}?output_format=... (mp3→mp3_44100_128, wav→pcm_44100,
ogg→ogg_44100). API key resolved via ctx.env at request time only (info()/estimate()
are key-free). estimate = text.length × per-character price for the resolved model
(request.model ?? config.defaultModel); unpriced models estimate $0.

```ts
export type Config = {
  apiKeyEnv: string;      // default "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY"
  baseUrl: string;        // default "https://api.elevenlabs.io"
  defaultModel: string;   // default "eleven_multilingual_v2"
  timeoutMs: number;      // default 60_000 (AbortSignal.timeout merged with caller signal)
  priceOverrides: Record<string, number>; // USD/char by model, merged over bundled table
};
export type State = { prices: Record<string, number> | null }; // lazy effective table

export type ElevenlabsApi = {
  info(): { provider: "elevenlabs"; configured: boolean; models: string[] }; // never throws
};

// Error classes (values in ElevenlabsErrors; types under Elevenlabs):
export class RetryableProviderError extends Error {
  readonly status: number | undefined;                 // 5xx or 429
  readonly kind: "timeout" | "network" | undefined;
  readonly retryAfterMs: number | undefined;           // parsed Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date)
  constructor(message: string,
    hint: { status?: number; kind?: "timeout" | "network"; retryAfterMs?: number });
}
export class TerminalProviderError extends Error {
  readonly status: number;                             // 4xx except 429
  constructor(message: string, status: number);
}
export class FlaggedProviderError extends Error {
  readonly kind: "content-policy" = "content-policy";
  constructor(message: string);
}
```

Bundled prices (USD/char): eleven_multilingual_v2 0.0003 · eleven_turbo_v2_5 0.000_15 ·
eleven_flash_v2_5 0.000_06 · eleven_monolingual_v1 0.0003.
Missing-key error (before any network call):
`[ai] ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is not set.\n  Export it or set config.apiKeyEnv to the variable that holds your key.`
Logs (redacted): elevenlabs:voiceover:done (info) / elevenlabs:voiceover:failed (warn).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.10 openai — app.openai (Complex tier; depends: [registryPlugin])
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Provider adapter via the official `openai` SDK (fetch-based; SDK retries disabled with
maxRetries: 0 — the runner owns retry timing). onInit registers THREE handlers:
("voiceover","openai") tts/handler.ts · ("translate","openai") translate/handler.ts ·
("prompt-gen","openai") prompt-gen/handler.ts. Lazy client (constructed on first
execute; info()/estimate() never touch it). Chat estimates use a chars/4 token
heuristic; actual cost is usage-based when reported, heuristic fallback otherwise.
Translate uses a fixed system prompt with temperature: 0 and never sets
detectedSourceLang. A non-null `refusal` in a chat response → FlaggedProviderError.
Voiceover format mapping: mp3→mp3 (audio/mpeg), wav→wav (audio/wav), ogg→opus (audio/ogg).

```ts
export type Config = {
  apiKeyEnv: string;                   // default "OPENAI_API_KEY"
  baseUrl?: string;                    // optional; proxies / OpenAI-compatible endpoints
  models: { tts: string; chat: string }; // default { tts: "gpt-4o-mini-tts", chat: "gpt-4o-mini" }
  timeoutMs: number;                   // default 60_000 (SDK client timeout)
  priceOverrides: Record<string, { inputPerM?: number; outputPerM?: number; ttsPerMChars?: number }>;
};
export type PriceTable = Record<string, { inputPerM?: number; outputPerM?: number; ttsPerMChars?: number }>;
export type State = { client: OpenaiClient | null; prices: PriceTable | null };

export type OpenaiApi = {
  info(): { provider: "openai"; configured: boolean; models: { tts: string; chat: string } };
};

// OpenaiClient is a STRUCTURAL alias covering exactly the two SDK calls used
// (audio.speech.create, chat.completions.create) — survives .d.ts bundling, trivially mockable.

// Error classes (values in OpenaiErrors; types under Openai) — same taxonomy shape:
export class RetryableProviderError extends Error {
  readonly status: number | undefined;
  readonly kind: "timeout" | "network" | undefined;
  readonly retryAfterMs: number | undefined;
  constructor(message: string,
    hint?: { status?: number; kind?: "timeout" | "network"; retryAfterMs?: number });
}
export class TerminalProviderError extends Error {
  readonly status: number | undefined;
  constructor(message: string, status?: number);
}
export class FlaggedProviderError extends Error { readonly kind = "content-policy" as const; }
```

Bundled prices: gpt-4o-mini $0.15/M in · $0.60/M out — gpt-4o $2.50/M in · $10/M out —
gpt-4o-mini-tts $15/M chars — tts-1 $15/M chars — tts-1-hd $30/M chars.
Missing-key error: `[ai] OPENAI_API_KEY is not set.\n  Export it or set config.apiKeyEnv
to the variable that holds your key.`
Logs (redacted): openai:{tts|translate|prompt-gen}:{done|failed}.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.11 codex — app.codex (Complex tier; depends: [registryPlugin])
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Image and prompt-gen provider over the local Codex CLI (`codex exec`). onInit registers
("image","codex") image/handler.ts, then ("prompt-gen","codex") prompt/handler.ts. Emits
no events. No API key: the CLI owns auth. Codex runs on the user's ChatGPT plan: images
are priced from a table whose bundled row is an explicit "gpt-6-astra": 0 (a model
without a price throws, it never counts as free); every prompt-gen result costs $0.
Registered after openai and before claude, fal and ark, so codex is the first image
provider (image.defaultProvider is "codex").

Per call, both tasks: a fresh temp dir `codex-*` under workDir (resolved against the cwd;
"" = os.tmpdir()), removed in `finally` on success and on every failure. Refs and images
are copied in as ref-<n>.<png|jpg|webp> (store paths have no extension and codex reads the
type from it; an unknown MIME is copied as png). The CLI is spawned with cwd <dir> and
stdin closed (an open stdin makes codex wait forever). timeoutMs → SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
5 s later; a caller abort kills the same way and rethrows signal.reason unchanged.

Image command (`--` is mandatory: --image is greedy and would take the prompt):

```
codex exec -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort="<effort>" --sandbox workspace-write
  --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir> -o <dir>/last-message.txt [--image <ref>]... -- <prompt>
```

- model = request.model ?? config.model; estimate = { usd: price of that model }.
- Prompt, one line each: "Generate exactly one image with your image generation tool.",
  request.prompt, "Avoid: <negative>." when set, the size line, a line naming the attached
  refs when there are any, then: save as output.png, no other files, reply with the file
  name only. Size line by aspect: "9:16" → "Portrait, 1024x1536." (also the default for a
  missing or unknown aspect), "16:9" → "Landscape, 1536x1024.", "1:1" → "Square, 1024x1024.".
- Result: output.png, else the newest .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp that is not a ref copy;
  mimeType by extension (image/png when unknown); meta { model, bytes }.

Prompt-gen command (never --output-schema: codex sends it as an OpenAI strict json_schema,
which rejects what z.toJSONSchema makes, so the schema travels in the prompt):

```
codex exec [-m <model>] -c model_reasoning_effort="<effort>" --sandbox read-only
  --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir> -o <dir>/last-message.txt [--image <abs path>]... -- <prompt>
```

- Prompt: codex has no system flag, so system, a blank line, then prompt. With a schema, a
  blank line, "Answer with one JSON value only, no prose, no code fence. It must match this
  JSON Schema:" and the schema as compact JSON.
- Answer: <dir>/last-message.txt, trimmed. With a schema: one ```json fence stripped,
  JSON.parse, checked with z.fromJSONSchema(schema); text is the validated JSON, re-stringified.
- params.images: ImageFile or ImageFile[], one --image each. params.responseSchema: a plain
  JSON-schema object. params.reasoning: "off" | "low" | "medium" | "high" (off → low;
  absent → config.reasoningEffort). temperature is ignored and listed in meta.ignored;
  cacheSystem and every other param are ignored. A bad images / responseSchema / reasoning
  throws a plain Error before any spawn, from estimate() too.
- messages, tools or toolChoice → PromptGenUnavailableError reason "unsupported", in
  estimate() and execute(), before any other work (see §4.6).
- estimate() validates the params and returns { usd: 0 }. execute() returns costUsd 0,
  toolCalls [], finishReason "stop", every usage count 0 (the CLI reports no tokens), and
  meta: CodexPromptMeta.
- Model mapping (request ids are OpenRouter style), in order: an exact modelMap entry; no
  request model → textModel; "openai/<id>" → "<id>"; a bare codex id (gpt-*, o<digit>*,
  codex-*) passes; anything else (e.g. "anthropic/claude-opus-5.5") → textModel. An empty
  textModel means no -m (codex's own default).

```ts
export type Config = {
  bin: string;              // default "codex" (bare name looked up on PATH, or a path)
  model: string;            // default "gpt-6-astra" (image model when a request names none)
  reasoningEffort: string;  // default "low" (-c model_reasoning_effort="<effort>", both tasks)
  timeoutMs: number;        // default 600_000 (kill the CLI after this long)
  workDir: string;          // default ".moku/tmp" (per-call temp dirs, against the cwd; "" = os.tmpdir())
  priceOverrides: Record<string, number>; // default {} (USD per image by model, merged over the bundled table)
  textModel: string;        // default "" (prompt-gen model when none maps; "" leaves -m out)
  modelMap: Record<string, string>; // default {} (exact request-model id → codex model, checked first)
};
export type State = { prices: Record<string, number> | null }; // effective table, computed at first use

export type CodexInfo = {
  provider: "codex";
  configured: boolean;      // config.bin exists: a path-like bin directly, a bare name on PATH (read via ctx.env)
  models: string[];         // models in the effective price table
};
export type CodexPromptMeta = {
  provider: "codex";
  model?: string;           // mapped -m; absent = codex's own default
  modelRequested?: string;  // request.model as the request named it
  effort: string;           // passed as -c model_reasoning_effort
  ignored?: string[];       // e.g. ["temperature"]
};
export type CodexApi = { info(): CodexInfo };  // no spawn

// Error classes (values in CodexErrors; types under Codex are aliases only) — no flagged class:
export class RetryableProviderError extends Error {
  readonly kind: "timeout" | "network";        // "timeout": the CLI ran past timeoutMs
  constructor(message: string, kind: "timeout" | "network");
}
export class TerminalProviderError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string);                // no status, no kind → runner class "unknown"
}
```

Errors (two-line messages, never the prompt):
- `[ai] No price for codex model "<m>".\n  Add it to codex priceOverrides.` (plain Error,
  estimate() and execute()).
- `[ai] Codex CLI not found: <bin>.\n  Install codex or set codex.bin.` (spawn ENOENT,
  PromptGenUnavailableError "missing").
- `[ai] Codex CLI is not logged in.\n  Run codex login, or use another provider.`
  (PromptGenUnavailableError "auth": API error status 401/403, or stderr matches
  /401 Unauthorized|not logged in|codex login/i).
- `[ai] Codex CLI hit its plan or rate limit.\n  Wait for the reset, or use another
  provider.` (PromptGenUnavailableError "limit": API error status 429, or stderr matches
  /usage limit|rate limit|\b429\b|too many requests/i).
- `[ai] Codex CLI could not start: <code>.\n  Check that codex.bin is an executable file.`
- `[ai] Codex exited with code <n>: <detail>.\n  Run the same codex exec by hand to see the
  full output.` (or "signal <name>"). detail = error.message of the API error codex prints
  as `ERROR: {…}` on stderr or as JSON on stdout, else the last stderr line; capped at 300
  chars. An API error with a status decides by status alone: any status other than
  401/403/429 (a 400 invalid_json_schema included) is terminal; one without a status is
  read by its wording.
- `[ai] Codex finished without writing an image.\n  Check that the codex model can generate
  images, then retry.` · `[ai] Codex wrote no answer.\n  Run the same codex exec by hand to
  see the full output.` · `[ai] Codex answer does not match params.responseSchema.\n  <path>:
  <issue>.` (or "The answer is not valid JSON.").
- `[ai] Codex timed out after <ms> ms.\n  Raise codex.timeoutMs or retry the build.`
  (RetryableProviderError kind "timeout").
- Param shape: `[ai] Codex params.images must be image files.`, `[ai] Codex
  params.responseSchema must be a JSON schema object.`, `[ai] Codex params.reasoning must
  be off, low, medium or high.`
Terminal and unavailable errors carry neither kind nor status, so the runner classifies
them "unknown" (terminal); promptGen.generate falls back only on the unavailable ones.
The framework sets no codex lane: image/codex and prompt-gen/codex use the limits
defaults; the README suggests capping a local CLI, e.g. "prompt-gen/codex": { concurrency: 2 }.
Logs: codex:image:done { model, bytes }, codex:prompt-gen:done { model ("default" when no
-m), chars }. The prompt and the answer are never logged.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.12 claude — app.claude (Complex tier; depends: [registryPlugin]; no state)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Text provider over the local Claude Code CLI (`claude -p --output-format json`). onInit
registers ("prompt-gen","claude") prompt/handler.ts. Emits no events. No API key: the CLI
owns auth. Plan-billed: costUsd is always 0; the CLI's own list price (total_cost_usd) is
kept in meta.listCostUsd for reference only. Registered after codex.

Per call: a fresh temp dir `moku-claude-*` under workDir ("" = os.tmpdir(), the default:
outside the repo, so no project CLAUDE.md is loaded), removed in `finally`. params.images
are copied in as image-<n>.<png|jpg|webp> (the Read tool needs an extension; an unknown
MIME is copied as png). The prompt goes to stdin, then stdin is closed; stdout is read in
full (the JSON result), stderr as a 4096-char tail. timeoutMs → SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 5 s
later; a caller abort kills the same way and rethrows signal.reason unchanged.

Command (the prompt is never in argv):

```
claude -p --output-format json --no-session-persistence --setting-sources user
  --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --system-prompt <request.system or default>
  --restricted --tools Read --allowedTools Read --permission-prompts none   (with images)
  --tools ""                                                                 (without images)
  [--model <mapped>] [--effort <low|medium|high>] [--json-schema <schema>]
```

- Default system prompt: "Answer the request directly. Output only the answer." It
  replaces Claude Code's coding-agent prompt. Never --bare: it disables OAuth, so plan
  billing breaks. --restricted confines the Read tool to the call dir.
- stdin text: request.prompt; with images, a blank line and "Attached images, read each
  with the Read tool before answering: ./image-1.png, …."; with a schema that cannot go to
  the flag, a blank line, the answer rule ("Answer with one JSON value only, no prose, no
  code fence. It must match this JSON Schema:") and the schema.
- params.responseSchema (a plain JSON-schema object) becomes compact JSON without a
  top-level $schema (the flag rejects that key). Root type "object" → --json-schema, and the
  answer is structured_output; any other root → in the prompt, and the answer is the result
  text with one ```json fence stripped. Either is checked with z.fromJSONSchema(schema);
  text is the validated JSON, re-stringified.
- params.reasoning "off" | "low" | "medium" | "high" → --effort (off → low); absent → no
  flag. params.images: ImageFile or ImageFile[]. temperature is ignored and listed in
  meta.ignored; cacheSystem and every other param are ignored. A bad images /
  responseSchema / reasoning throws a plain Error before any spawn, from estimate() too.
- messages, tools or toolChoice → PromptGenUnavailableError reason "unsupported", in
  estimate() and execute(), before any other work (see §4.6).
- estimate() validates the params and returns { usd: 0 }. execute() returns costUsd 0,
  toolCalls [], finishReason "stop" and typed usage: promptTokens = input_tokens +
  cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens, completionTokens = output_tokens,
  cachedTokens = cache_read_input_tokens, cacheWriteTokens = cache_creation_input_tokens
  (0 when unreported); cachedReadTokens / cachedWriteTokens only when the CLI reports them.
- Model mapping, in order: an exact modelMap entry; no request model → textModel;
  "anthropic/<id>" → prefix stripped, dots to dashes ("anthropic/claude-opus-5.5" →
  "claude-opus-5-5"); a bare claude-*, opus, sonnet, haiku or fable passes; anything else
  (e.g. "openai/gpt-6-sol") → textModel. An empty textModel means no --model (the CLI's
  default).

```ts
export type Config = {
  bin: string;          // default "claude" (bare name looked up on PATH, or a path)
  textModel: string;    // default "" (model when mapping gives none; "" = no --model)
  modelMap: Record<string, string>; // default {} (exact request-model id → claude model, checked first)
  timeoutMs: number;    // default 600_000 (kill the CLI, SIGTERM, after this long)
  workDir: string;      // default "" (per-call temp dirs; "" = os.tmpdir(), outside the repo)
};
export type Reasoning = "off" | "low" | "medium" | "high"; // params.reasoning
export type Effort = "low" | "medium" | "high";            // --effort

export type ClaudePromptMeta = {
  provider: "claude";
  model?: string;           // mapped --model; absent = the CLI's default
  modelRequested?: string;  // request.model as the request named it
  effort?: Effort;          // only when --effort was passed
  listCostUsd: number;      // total_cost_usd, reference only (the plan bills $0)
  usage: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number };
  ignored?: string[];       // e.g. ["temperature"]
};
export type ClaudeInfo = {
  provider: "claude";
  configured: boolean;      // config.bin exists: a path-like bin directly, a bare name on PATH (read via ctx.env)
};
export type ClaudeApi = { info(): ClaudeInfo };  // no spawn

// Error classes (values in ClaudeErrors; types under Claude are aliases only) — no flagged class:
export class RetryableProviderError extends Error {
  readonly kind: "timeout" | "network";        // "timeout": the CLI ran past timeoutMs
  constructor(message: string, kind: "timeout" | "network");
}
export class TerminalProviderError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string);                // no status, no kind → runner class "unknown"
}
```

Errors (stdout JSON is parsed first, even on a non-zero exit: the not-logged-in result
exits 1 with valid JSON; two-line messages, never the prompt):
- `[ai] Claude CLI not found: <bin>.\n  Install Claude Code or set claude.bin.` (spawn
  ENOENT, PromptGenUnavailableError "missing").
- `[ai] Claude CLI is not logged in.\n  Run claude and /login, or use another provider.`
  (PromptGenUnavailableError "auth": text matches /not logged in|\/login|invalid api key/i
  or api_error_status 401/403).
- `[ai] Claude CLI hit its plan or rate limit.\n  Wait for the reset, or use another
  provider.` (PromptGenUnavailableError "limit": text matches /usage limit|limit
  reached|hit your limit|rate limit/i or api_error_status 429). Both patterns read the
  is_error result, or stderr when stdout is not JSON.
- `[ai] Claude CLI could not start: <code>.\n  Check that claude.bin is an executable file.`
- `[ai] Claude returned an error: <first line, max 200 chars>.\n  Run the same claude -p by
  hand to see the full output.` (is_error true, not auth or limit).
- `[ai] Claude exited with code <n>: <last stderr line>.` (or "signal <name>"; no JSON) ·
  `[ai] Claude printed no JSON result.` (exit 0, no JSON) · `[ai] Claude wrote no answer.`
  (blank result, no structured_output). Each adds `\n  Run the same claude -p by hand to
  see the full output.` · `[ai] Claude answer does not match
  params.responseSchema.\n  <path>: <issue>.` (or "The answer is not valid JSON.").
- `[ai] Claude timed out after <ms> ms.\n  Raise claude.timeoutMs or retry the build.`
  (RetryableProviderError kind "timeout").
- Param shape: `[ai] Claude params.images must be image files.`, `[ai] Claude
  params.responseSchema must be a JSON schema object.`, `[ai] Claude params.reasoning must
  be off, low, medium or high.`
promptGen.generate falls back only on the unavailable errors; it rethrows the rest. The
"prompt-gen/claude" lane caps how many local claude processes run at once (limits
defaults unless set). Logs: claude:prompt-gen:done { model ("default" when no --model),
chars }. The prompt and the answer are never logged.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.13 compose — app.compose (Standard tier; depends: [buildfilePlugin, promptGenPlugin])
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Natural-language prompt → validated build file. Pipeline: system prompt embedding
buildfile.jsonSchema() + per-task input docs → promptGen.generate({ prompt, system },
{ provider, signal }) → strip defensive ```yaml fence → buildfile.compile({ text,
lang: "yaml" }) → on failure re-prompt with the validation issue, up to
maxRepairAttempts additional times → apply opts.name override → emit. GUARANTEE:
compose can never return an invalid build file. Never writes files — the CLI (or the
caller) persists `text`. Never touches registry (the audited cast stays with the task
plugin). costUsd accumulates across ALL attempts, failed ones included.

```ts
export type Config = {
  provider: string;          // default "openai" — passed to promptGen.generate
  maxRepairAttempts: number; // default 2 — ADDITIONAL attempts; total = 1 + maxRepairAttempts
};
export type ComposeResult = { spec: BuildSpec; text: string; costUsd: number };
export type ComposeApi = {
  compose(opts: {
    prompt: string;
    emit: "build" | "script"; // "build" = YAML (modeline + $schema key); "script" = defineBuild() TS module
    name?: string;            // spec.name override, applied after validation
    signal?: AbortSignal;     // forwarded to every promptGen.generate call
  }): Promise<ComposeResult>;
};
```

Exhaustion error: `[ai] Compose could not produce a valid build file after <n> attempts.
  Refine the prompt or write the build file manually with "moku new".`

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.14 cli — app.cli (Complex tier; depends: [runnerPlugin, buildfilePlugin, composePlugin])
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The `moku` command surface: 7 commands (new, validate, estimate, run, export, status,
compose). No lifecycle, no state (ratified OQ1). `--config` is read and stripped by the
bin (see §1), never by dispatch. argv parsed with
node:util parseArgs (strict; kebab flags → camelCase keys; boolean flags recorded as
the literal "true"). All rendering through @moku-labs/common/cli's BrandConsole (MC1);
plain mode when config.plain || !TTY || NO_COLOR (via ctx.env). dispatch() NEVER calls
process.exit — src/bin.ts owns the process (createApp → start → dispatch → stop → exit).
SIGINT wiring (run/compose): first Ctrl-C aborts the AbortSignal (clean pause/drain);
the once-listener then falls through to Node's default on a second Ctrl-C.

```ts
export type Config = { plain: boolean }; // default false

export const EXIT_CODES = {
  ok: 0, failure: 1, validation: 2, usage: 3, paused: 4, budgetStop: 5
} as const;

export type CliApi = {
  dispatch(argv: string[]): Promise<number>; // argv excludes node/script prefix
  commands(): CommandTree;                    // mountable tree for a future umbrella CLI
};
export type CommandTree = {
  name: string; description: string;
  commands: Array<{ name: string; description: string; flags: Record<string, string> }>;
};
// Also exported under the Cli namespace: CommandContext, CommandDefinition,
// CommandFlags, CommandFlagSpec.
```

Commands:
- moku new [name] — writes template({ name }) to <name>.moku.yaml (default "build") +
  jsonSchema() at the modeline path; refuses overwrite (exit 1).
- moku validate [glob] — loadGlob; exit 0 all valid, 2 on first invalid/empty match.
- moku estimate [glob] — runner.estimate breakdown box; exit 0.
- moku run [glob] [--max-cost <usd>] [--dry-run] [--out <dir>] [--flat] — runner.run +
  events() progress, then runner.export({ runId, outDir: --out ?? "out", flat }) (not on
  --dry-run); exits: done→0, failed→1, paused→4, budget-stopped→5, bad --max-cost→3.
- moku export [runId] [--out <dir>] [--flat] — runner.export of the given (or newest) run
  to <out>/<build>/<label>.<ext>, or <out>/<label>.<ext> with --flat (default out "out");
  a skipped label is listed as "skipped: unsafe name or duplicate target". Exit 0, 1 when
  the export throws.
- moku status [runId] [--follow] — status snapshot; --follow polls
  journal.readSnapshot every 1s (short-lived reads — WAL checkpoint-starvation
  mitigation) until terminal. Exit 0.
- moku compose "<prompt>" [--emit build|script] [--out <path>] — compose.compose;
  writes --out or prints; exits 0 ok, 3 usage, 2 repair-exhausted, else 1.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.15 asset — app.asset (Standard tier; depends: [registryPlugin]; stateless)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Owns the "asset" task contract: register ONE portrait with a provider, in the
provider's own account, and get back an opaque AssetRecord. Registration is its own
build item that runs BEFORE any video item that uses it — never a retry after a
refusal, never a fallback to the raw photo. The done item's stored artifact is the
AssetRecord JSON under ASSET_MIME; a video item `$ref`s it and the runner hands the
video handler a file with mimeType === ASSET_MIME. Ordering, dedupe, resume and reuse
come from the runner/journal/store (no new tables); the only runner change is one MIME
entry so an exported record is `<label>.json`. contract.ts imports nothing.

```ts
export const ASSET_MIME = "application/vnd.moku.asset+json";
export type AssetFile = { path: string; mimeType: string; hash: string };
export type AssetGroupKind = "aigc";               // only kind in v1
export type AssetRequest = {
  image: AssetFile;          // its sha256 hash is part of the artifact key
  url?: string;              // public https URL of the same bytes (Ark CreateAsset fetches URLs only)
  group?: AssetGroupKind;    // default "aigc"
  name?: string;             // display name, max 64 chars; default: the file's base name
```
